---

### Adding a new item

1. **Summarize** the request into a clear, scannable entry. Match the style of existing
   entries — a short bold title, then a dash and explanation with enough context to
   understand later.
2. **Find references**: search `docs/plans/` and `docs/` for related files. If a relevant
   plan exists, link it as `[plan](docs/plans/...)`.
3. **If an in-progress plan** exists in the conversation or at `.claude/plans/`, write it
   to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` first, then link it.
4. **Rank it 0–5** against the rubric below and put the tier in the marker.
5. Format: `- [T<n>] **Title** — explanation. [plan](docs/plans/...) or [docs/path](docs/path)`
   - Plans: `[plan](docs/plans/2026-03-21-foo.md)`
   - Other docs: filename as link text
6. **Where to place**: under the most relevant `###` subsection inside `## Open`. If
   none fits, create a new `###` subsection. Default to `### Housekeeping`.
7. Place after the last open item in that subsection (before the next `###`/`##` header).
8. Use backtick formatting for code, paths, and commands. Use `[text](path)` links.
9. **Do NOT leave any `[x]` items in `## Open`** — the PostToolUse hook will block
   the write if you do. If you encounter one while editing, move it to Done
   at the same time.
10. **Report the rank and a one-line reason** in your reply, so a bad call is visible
    immediately rather than discovered when the work is dispatched.

---

### Ranking rubric (tiers)

Rank by how much *thinking* the task needs, not how long it takes. Canonical table lives
in `~/CLAUDE.md` — Delegation.

| Tier | Kind of work | Dispatched to |
|---|---|---|
| **T0** | Mechanical lookup — grep, find, count, "which file defines X". No judgment. | `t0-lookup` (haiku, read-only) |
| **T1** | Mechanical edit with a known recipe — rename, version bump, apply a diagnosed fix. | `t1-sonnet-med` |
| **T2** | Bounded implementation — one file/module, clear spec, judgment about *how* not *what*. | `t2-sonnet-high` |
| **T3** | Multi-file work against a settled plan. **Default when unranked.** | `t3-opus-med` |
| **T4** | Design *and* implementation — non-obvious architecture, unknown root cause. | `t4-opus-high` |
| **T5** | Do it yourself, inline — judgment the user cares about, plan decisions, final review. | *(no agent)* |

When genuinely torn between two tiers, take the **higher** one: over-ranking wastes
tokens, under-ranking produces a confident wrong edit.

---

### Ranking an unranked file

When `$ARGUMENTS` is `rank`: assign a tier to every **unranked open item** in `TODO.md`.

1. Read every open item — `- [ ]`, and any `[wip]`/`[verify]` with no tier.
2. Rank each against the rubric. Use the linked plan for context where one exists.
3. Leave already-ranked items **exactly as they are**. This is additive only.
4. Leave the auto-captured deferrals inbox (the `<!-- BEGIN auto-captured-deferrals -->`
   block) alone — those are untriaged by design and `audit-plan-deferrals.sh` owns them.
5. Make **ONE Write** of the whole file, not many small edits.
6. Report a tier histogram (`T0×2 T1×5 T2×3 T3×8 T4×1 T5×0`) and call out anything you
   ranked T4/T5, since those are the expensive calls worth a second opinion.

---

### Moving an item to Watch

When something needs periodic checking rather than active work (monitor for upstream changes, check before releases, act only if a threshold is crossed):

1. Remove the `- [ ]` item from `## Open`.
2. Add a plain bullet under the appropriate `###` subsection in `## Watch`. Create the subsection if needed.
3. Include what to check, how often/when, and what action to take if the trigger fires.

To promote: move from `## Watch` back to `## Open` as a `- [ ]` item when the trigger fires.

---

### Parking an item

When something is intentionally shelved (feasibility study done but not starting, blocked on external factor, future-phase work):

1. Remove the `- [ ]` item from `## Open`.
2. Add a plain bullet (no checkbox) under the appropriate `###` subsection in `## Parked`. Create the subsection if needed.
3. Keep the description concise — strip "PARKED —" prefixes and "not started" boilerplate.

To unpark: move from `## Parked` back to a `## Open` `###` subsection as a `- [ ]` item.

---

### Marking an item done

When the user says "done: <title>" or a task has just been completed:

1. Find the item's line in `## Open` (any open marker — `[ ]`, `[T3]`, `[wip T2]`, `[verify T3]`).
2. **Remove it** from `## Open` entirely (do not change it to `[x]` in place).
3. Add a one-line entry at the **top** of `## Done` (right after the `## Done` header):
   ```
   - [x] YYYY-MM-DD — [slug] Short description of what was done (~130 chars max). See [plan](path).
   ```
   - `slug`: kebab-case short ID, e.g. `vendor-task`, `package-tilemap`
   - Date: today's date (from `date -u +%F` if needed)
   - Description: tight summary of the outcome, not the original task wording
   - Link the plan or doc if one exists
4. **Drop the tier** — Done lines are `[x]` with no `T<n>`. The tier is a dispatch input,
   not a historical record, and the line is already length-capped.
5. **Strip any `<!-- agent:… -->` stamp.** The agent is done holding that context; leaving
   the stamp would invite a future `/next` to re-message a dead agent.

**Never** mark an item `[x]` in `## Open` — always delete from Open and insert into Done.

---

### Sweeping (cleanup / bulk migrate)

When `$ARGUMENTS` is `sweep` or `cleanup`: reconcile the whole file into the four-bucket
model in one pass. Use this to migrate a legacy TODO (topical sections, `- [x]` scattered
inline) or to tidy drift.

1. **Classify every item** by its current marker and wording, then route it:
   - `- [x]`, `- [cancelled]`, `- [investigated → DONE]` → **`## Done`**.
   - `- [ ]`, `- [~]` / `- [wip]` (in-progress), `- [verify]` → **`## Open`** (under a `###`
     subsection; reuse the originating topical section name as the subsection,
     kebab-or-titled). **Normalise `[~]` to `[wip]`** — `[wip]` is the canonical spelling.
   - Items whose text says *defer / parked / blocked on / future-phase / trigger: when X* →
     **`## Parked`** (plain bullet, strip "PARKED —"/"not started" boilerplate).
   - Items whose text says *monitor / watch / check before release / act if threshold* →
     **`## Watch`** (plain bullet, with the trigger condition).
   - When genuinely unsure between Open and Parked, prefer **Open** (don't silently shelve work).
2. **Done lines** use the standard one-line form, newest first:
   `- [x] YYYY-MM-DD — [slug] short description (~130 chars max). See [plan](path).`
   - Derive the date from: an explicit `DONE YYYY-MM-DD` in the entry → the linked plan's
     date prefix (`docs/plans/2026-06-13-…` → `2026-06-13`) → `git log -1 --format=%cs <commit>`
     for a cited hash → `????-??-??` if none can be found (never invent one; flag it).
   - `slug`: the plan/topic slug, else a kebab of the originating section.
   - The full detail stays in the linked plan/commit, so the short line is lossless.
3. **Prune emptied structure**: delete any heading (and its intro prose) left with no items.
4. **Rank everything that lands in `## Open`** — a sweep is also a `rank` pass. Done lines
   drop their tier; Watch and Parked bullets never carry one.
5. After writing, run `task md -- TODO.md` if available, then report: counts moved to each
   bucket, the tier histogram, any dates that fell back to `????-??-??`, and which empty
   sections you removed.

This is a large structural rewrite — make ONE Write of the whole file, not many small edits.

---

### Format rules (all operations)

- The four top-level sections are fixed: `## Open`, `## Watch`, `## Parked`, `## Done`. Do not add others.
- `## Open` → `###` subsections → open items only. No `[x]` items ever, tiered or not.
- `## Watch` → `###` subsections → plain `- ` bullets (what to check + trigger condition).
- `## Parked` → `###` subsections → plain `- ` bullets (no checkbox). No `[x]` items.
- `## Done` → flat list of `- [x] YYYY-MM-DD — [slug] …` lines, newest first, **no tier**.
- Backticks for code/paths/commands. Relative `[text](path)` links, never bare paths.

**Marker grammar.** The status bracket carries status *and* delegation tier, tier last,
both optional. Canonical parser: `TASK_RE` in `~/python-tui-lib/tuilib/todo_format.py`.

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `- [ ]` | open, unranked — dispatched at the `T3` default |
| `- [T4]` | open, tier 4 |
| `- [wip T2]` | in progress, tier 2 |
| `- [verify T3]` | implemented, verification not yet run + recorded |
| `- [x]` | done — `## Done` only |

**Agent stamp.** While an item is `[wip …]`, `/next` stamps the dispatched agent's id on
it as `<!-- agent:a7a12a1f88b6840b4 -->`. It renders invisibly and survives compaction, so
a later `/next` can `SendMessage` that agent instead of briefing a fresh one. Preserve it
on any edit to a `[wip …]` line; strip it when the item moves to Done.
